profile.reading:
Per Vantage Data Centers' own facility page, this campus is located at 45 S Bullard Avenue, Goodyear, AZ 85338; Vantage markets the campus as "Phoenix," though the confirmed address places it in Goodyear, a separate West Valley suburb. Vantage describes the campus as 50 acres with more than 1 million square feet at full buildout, five data centers planned, and 176 megawatts of critical IT load, delivered via a 69-plus kilovolt incoming feed distributed at 12kV and 480V with N+1 power redundancy (mechanical N+2 planned). Two buildings, AZ11 and AZ12, are individually cited on the page as each achieving Green Globe for New Construction certification from the Green Building Initiative; a third building, AZ13, is confirmed to exist by third-party trackers but is not individually named on Vantage's own page.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Phoenix-area utilities have faced sustained strain from data center growth: Arizona Public Service has said it received 19 gigawatts of electrical service requests from data centers and large commercial users it currently cannot serve, with individual requests now averaging about 500 megawatts each; APS filed for a nearly 14% residential rate increase expected no earlier than July 2026, and SRP raised rates in November 2025, including a 50% increase in fixed monthly charges for single-family homes.

Arizona's West Valley, including Goodyear, has become one of the fastest-growing U.S. data center corridors alongside Mesa, Phoenix, and Chandler, drawing Vantage alongside Meta, Google, Microsoft, and EdgeConneX. Arizona Public Service and Salt River Project have both signed large-load interconnection agreements with data center developers in the West Valley, and APS has periodically flagged transmission capacity constraints in Buckeye and Goodyear as a factor pacing new project timelines. Water use is a live regulatory issue in the Phoenix metro generally, since Arizona's Department of Water Resources designates the area an Active Management Area with assured-supply requirements, and large air-cooled or hybrid-cooled data centers have drawn attention from Goodyear city council and state legislators weighing the tradeoff between data center tax revenue, jobs, and long-term aquifer strain in a desert climate.

reading.body:
This Vantage campus in Goodyear, Arizona spans five buildings totaling more than one million square feet across 50 acres. The operator publishes 176 MW of critical IT load for the entire campus. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this campus could house roughly 4,400 racks, though the operator's stated average power density of 250 W per square foot suggests the actual mix of workloads and equipment may differ from that assumption.

Two of the five buildings, AZ11 and AZ12, hold Green Globe certification for new construction through the Green Building Initiative. The certification qualifies those structures for environmentally managed occupancy but does not specify their individual capacities or which tenants occupy them. Arizona has four facilities with published power specifications totaling 512 MW across the state, and this campus ranks fifth by that measure, though it represents a significant share of disclosed capacity in a state where most of 56 mapped facilities do not publish figures.

The campus sits outside Phoenix in a region where grid constraints may affect future expansion. The operator's own page describes the campus as current and active across its five buildings, implying all are operational or available. No published information confirms which AI training, inference, or other workloads occupy these buildings, or what fraction of the 176 MW is currently in use.
